groups.title: Tablet (D39500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold, such as sore throat, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have or have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine); or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol or flucloxacillin.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, or, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body or on the mouth or eye membranes), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E04600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during growth and in old age, for poor development of the bones and teeth, for the prevention of rickets, for beriberi and eye strain, for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis, and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 8 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have high blood calcium, sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause) or kidney disease; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have kidney stones or severe renal failure; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria (excessive excretion of oxalate in the urine); if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gout; or if you have or have had kidney stones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may interfere with the detection of sugar in various urine tests, and it may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation, an antacid, levodopa or an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, loose stools, loss of appetite, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary oedema, or menstruation coming earlier than expected, becoming heavier or bleeding for longer occurs, or if you are short of folic acid, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C and of zinc, poor bone and tooth development, prevention of rickets, beriberi, eye strain, neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis

groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, oedema, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, or if you take it together with a potassium-containing preparation, a liquorice-containing preparation, a preparation containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, a loop diuretic (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or a thiazide diuretic (trichlormethiazide). Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver function disorder (general lassitude, jaundice), interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever), pseudoaldosteronism or myopathy occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (E44900ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of constipation and of the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that follow constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 to 3 tablets per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 2/3 to 2 tablets per dose. groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger; if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel); or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child aged 10 years or younger; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not chew the tablet when taking it. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.caution:

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose dexibuprofen (1,200 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors such as high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes or smoking who need high-dose ibuprofen must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.
